style_when: the article is a purely conceptual synthesis or policy dilemma where no physical facility, machine, or supply chain exists, and an elegant abstract paper silhouette states the idea. Never reach for paper collage when the story describes physical manufacturing, freight, energy, hardware, or heavy infrastructure — use cinematic still or telephoto industry instead
prompt: Minimalist editorial cut-paper collage on a warm oak home office desk. Two stylized cut-paper object silhouettes: a bone white stock certificate with a prominent clean void cut from its center, layered over a graphite data-rack silhouette. Hand-torn rag paper with visible fibre, physical cast shadows under each crisp layer, one raking directional light from the left. Muted modern editorial palette of bone white, graphite, and ochre. Extreme asymmetry, crisp clean edges, generous negative space, no bare geometry, no text, no legible print.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, typography, watermarks, 3d render, people
rationale: The article explores a conceptual financial dilemma—the 'buyback gap' and capital reallocation—which is perfectly captured by an abstract, high-contrast paper collage emphasizing the missing equity piece.
subject: cut-paper silhouette of a stock certificate with a central void
core_thesis: The corporate buyer that historically absorbed employee stock grants has stopped bidding, leaving a visible gap in the de-risking trade.
core_conflict: Massive capital expenditure on AI computing equipment vs. traditional share buybacks for equity holders.
